name: pdk-verdaccio-uplink-refresh-without-clobbering
instr:
# Shared uplink metadata on a Verdaccio cluster

## Goal
Three Verdaccio processes share one filesystem-backed storage directory while proxying an npm registry and accepting private releases of the same package names. Support a coherent shared cache: each process should see the same local releases and uplink metadata without redundant fetches or unbounded stale responses.

## Requirements
1. A package fetched from the uplink remains available at `GET /<package>` alongside versions published locally through `PUT /<package>`; the local versions' metadata and their dist-tags remain intact. A local publish on another node completes within 2.5 seconds while an uplink response is delayed, without losing its version or tags when the refresh finishes. An upstream dist-tag must not replace a locally published value for that tag.
2. Once an uplink entry's configured `maxage` expires, 30 concurrent requests on all three processes sharing storage cause at most one upstream metadata request for that package; subsequent requests within `maxage` use the shared refreshed entry.
3. Support an uplink setting `max_stale_if_error` using Verdaccio's duration notation. When upstream metadata is unavailable, return a cached package only while the time since its last successful fetch is less than this budget; at or beyond the budget return HTTP 503. The deployment uses `maxage: 5s` and `max_stale_if_error: 10s`. A successful revalidation renews the freshness timestamp.
